Option 1: "چون سحر آخر پر پرواز خواهد شد قفس - تا توانی صبر کن بیدل درین کلفت سرا"

Rough translation: "Like the last dawn, the cage will fly away—until you can, be patient, dear one, in this heavy house." It seems about hope that the cage (imprisonment) will be freed by dawn, urging patience. Concept: hope, liberation, patience.

Option 2: "همه پر زهره و برجیس و قمر خواهد شد - چون فلک روی زمین از سمن و سوسن وگل"

Translation: "All will become Venus, Jupiter, and the moon—like the heavens on earth from sandalwood and lily and flower." This seems about beauty, celestial bodies, perhaps praising beauty or describing a scene. Concept: beauty, celestial imagery.

Option 3: "اشک نشوید این گلیم تا شب من سحر شوم - بخت سیه چو دود شمع چترزده است برسرم"

Translation: "Do not shed tears, this shawl, until the night I become dawn—my fate is dark as a smoldering candle's smoke." This seems about despair, warning not to cry; gloom. Concept: gloom, sorrow.

Option 4: "بر خدا دل نه که خوش خوش کام شادی هم رسد - خسروا ناخوش مشو کایامِ شادی درگذشت"

Translation: "By God, don't be heartless that happiness comes easily—don't be unhappy, O, because joy has passed." This seems about not being unhappy because joy has passed. Concept: lamentation about lost joy.
